title: Optimize quant kernels: fuse dequant + smoothquant paths and scheduler tweaks for INT8/FP8
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Quantized inference for production workloads at Redwood needs lower tail latency and higher throughput while preserving model quality. Previous paths handled smoothquant preprocessing and dequantization as separate kernel invocations which created unnecessary copies and fragmented compute; INT8 and FP8 flows diverged early causing suboptimal kernel selection and scheduling. This PR fuses dequant + smoothquant into unified execution paths for INT8 and FP8, adds a kernel-selection optimization in the runtime compiler to prefer fused kernels when input statistics match, and tweaks the scheduler to prefer continuous-batching affinity for small interactive requests. Summary of changes: 1) Add fused kernels: runtime/quant/kernels/fused_dequant_smoothquant_int8.cpp and fused_dequant_smoothquant_fp8.cpp implementing in-place dequant + smoothquant with attention to alignment and vectorized paths. 2) Kernel registration: runtime/quant/fusion/registry.cc with new heuristics to pick fused kernels based on per-model scaling stats and runtime env (GPU compute capability). 3) Compiler selection: compiler/kernel_selector.cc updated to prefer fused kernels when quant-scale variance < threshold (configurable). 4) Scheduler tweaks: runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching.cc changes to keep affinity for short requests that benefit from fused kernels and to reduce context-switch overhead for KV cache hits. 5) Add microbenchmarks and integration perf tests: bench/bench_quant.py and tests/quant/test_fused_kernels.py. 6) Documentation: docs/perf/quant-kernels.md describing heuristics and rollout guidance. Motivation: reduce memory traffic and kernel launch overhead, unify INT8/FP8 code paths to unlock vectorized kernels and reduce branching in hot loops. Benchmarks: on internal Llama-2-13B INT8 profile with realistic prompt distribution we measured median token latency down 8-15% and throughput up 12-22% on A10G provisioning; FP8 path saw 6-11% median latency reduction and 9-14% throughput improvement. KV-cache-heavy conversational workload saw 10-18% end-to-end latency improvement due to scheduler affinity changes. Quality: numeric validation against existing float baselines and dequant-only paths shows max per-token logit drift within 1e-3 in L2 for tested models; we ran the existing eval harness and saw no regression in generation quality for our canary prompt set. Implementation notes: fused kernels attempt in-place transformation to avoid extra buffer allocation; when alignment constraints prevent in-place ops we fall back to the previous dequant path. The kernel selection threshold is tunable via redwood.conf under [quantization] fused_threshold and defaults to conservative value used in benchmarks. Tests and CI: added unit tests for fused kernel correctness (elementwise outputs vs reference), stress tests to exercise alignment edge cases, and perf microbenchmarks. CI flakiness: an integration GPU test failed once due to a transient driver scheduling issue (CI job gpu-integration/linux/1) which was rerun and passed; all CI gates green before merging. Rollout and safety: feature gated behind runtime flag --enable-fused-quant-kernels and disabled by default for older GPU types (compute capability < 7.5); opt-in via runtime config in Dedicated/Private. Observability: added metrics quant.fused_kernel_hits and quant.fused_kernel_misses and trace tags to attribute fused kernel selection to model/scenario. Migration: operators should see no API changes; recommend canary rollout with 1-5% traffic on dedicated clusters to validate before scaling. Checklist: [x] unit tests added, [x] perf numbers collected and reproducible, [x] docs updated, [x] feature gated, [x] added metrics, [x] reviewers sign-off. Related: builds on prior work in ENG-1987 (continuous batching improvements) and ENG-2123 (quant kernel refactor).

release_notes: Performance: Fused dequant+smoothquant kernels for INT8/FP8 reduce latency and increase throughput for quantized inference.
Feature: New runtime flag --enable-fused-quant-kernels and config [quantization].fused_threshold to control kernel selection.
Observability: Added quant.fused_kernel_hits and quant.fused_kernel_misses metrics.
notes: Recommended rollout: enable on canary Dedicated clusters, validate perf and quality metrics, then progressively increase traffic. Backout: set --enable-fused-quant-kernels=false or adjust fused_threshold to 0 to disable fused path.
